On Fri, May 3, 2013 at 2:16 AM, Dhanasekaran Anbalagan <bugc...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Guys,

We are currently using rmr2. for our internal application analysis. We are using all files .csv files it's size also very low, likely below MB.

For text files I would recommend concatenating them, with the filename as an added field. A simple mapreduce program can do that. To know which filename you are reading, call Sys.getenv("map_input_file"). Something like

mapreduce(input = dir-with-csv-files, output = dir-for-concatenated-files, map = function(k,v) cbind(fname = Sys.getenv("map_input_file"), input.format = make.input.format("csv", other-args-to-read.table))

I've never tried it so test it with care, in particular the number of output partitions will depend on several factors and I am not sure what it's going to be.

When starting face we allotted 5GB. currently now 12GB.  When I tired googled it's give me nice link. they implemented HAR file format.
http://blog.cloudera.com/blog/2009/02/the-small-files-problem/
As they say, as this time HAR is mostly for archival purposes (nice way to say: useless). They recommend concatenating or merging into sequence file,
can you anyone guide it's some other mechanism to solve the small file issue. when analysis lot of small file occupy the Heap memory.
This part is unclear, you'll have to explain it a little better for me to say anything

-Dhanasekaran.

Did I learn something today? If not, I wasted it.

Not yet, but I am hopeful.
